turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call. Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Start there.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Meredith: Don't thank me yet. Owen's English teacher doesn't enter a zero before he calls the parent. Who decided that was the right order?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

Meredith: A machine's guess. Ninety-four percent of what, and who checked it? Turnitin's own guide says that indicator shouldn't be the sole basis for an adverse action against a student. Is it the sole basis, Mr. Hale?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
Meredith: "Quite reliable." Okay. Reliable at what, and what else do you have besides the score?
So I had to give him a zero.
Meredith: "Had to." Procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. So you didn't have to. You chose it, and you did it before you called me.
I hope you understand my position.
Meredith: I understand your position perfectly well. You're a teacher who entered a mark before checking it. What evidence do you have that Owen wrote anything other than what he handed in?
